_help: Reference pages. 'wordFamilies' is the Word family page (Track A). 'hedgingBank' is the Hedging bank page (Track B). Each group has a title, a short note, a list of entries and one example sentence. Edit the text between the quotation marks.

wordFamilies.title: -tion / -sion
wordFamilies.example: The introduction of online classes led to a reduction in travel.

wordFamilies.title: -ment
wordFamilies.example: Greater investment in schools can lead to an improvement in results.

wordFamilies.title: -ance / -ence / -ency
wordFamilies.note: Adjectives ending in -ant / -ent, and some verbs.
wordFamilies.example: Regular attendance is linked to better performance.

wordFamilies.title: -ity
wordFamilies.example: The availability of cheap flights has increased the complexity of travel rules.

wordFamilies.title: -sis / -ysis
wordFamilies.note: Often from verbs ending in -yse or -ise.
wordFamilies.example: Careful analysis of the data supports this hypothesis.

wordFamilies.title: -al / -ure
wordFamilies.note: A smaller group, but common in essays.
wordFamilies.example: The closure of the factory followed the failure of the business.

wordFamilies.title: -ness / -th / -acy / -iour
wordFamilies.example: Rapid growth can reduce the accuracy of forecasts.

hedgingBank.title: Modal verbs
hedgingBank.note: Put them before the main verb.
hedgingBank.example: Online learning may improve access to education.

hedgingBank.title: Reporting and other cautious verbs
hedgingBank.note: Use them to report evidence without saying it proves something.
hedgingBank.example: The results suggest that sleep affects memory.

hedgingBank.title: Adverbs
hedgingBank.note: They change how sure the whole claim sounds.
hedgingBank.example: This is probably the main reason for the change.

hedgingBank.title: Adjectives
hedgingBank.note: Often used with “it is … that” or “a … cause”.
hedgingBank.example: It is likely that prices will rise next year.

hedgingBank.title: Quantity and frequency words
hedgingBank.note: They limit how many or how often.
hedgingBank.example: Many students find group work useful.

hedgingTip: One hedge is usually enough. “may possibly perhaps suggest” is too weak and hard to read. Match the strength of your claim to the evidence.
